title: CARET beta-carotene and retinol trial: lung-cancer-prevention intervention halted for no benefit and harm
summary: The Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial is promoted as a prevention-trial negative-result/harm record. CARET was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of beta-carotene plus retinyl palmitate in 18,314 people at high risk for lung cancer because of smoking history or asbestos exposure. The intervention was halted early with definitive evidence of no benefit and substantial evidence of harm, including increased lung-cancer incidence and total mortality.
